suggestion.problemOrOpportunity: DotLn's Codex launches inherit the operator's Codex home. That covers the product worker transport and six probe scripts. The tracked diagnosis attributes 36 of 43 user-level trust entries to ten DotLn scratch and probe families. WO-111 closed only on an operator waiver of its outside-portfolio clause, and WO-111-D011 asks that no further live Codex worker proof run before an isolation order. No executable check enforces that. The next critical-path step puts live Codex workers on owner repositories, where a trust entry also admits project-local configuration, hooks and rules.
suggestion.scope: Build one shared Codex launcher, used by worker-transport.ts and the six probe scripts. For each episode it supplies an isolated Codex home, with authentication available and no credentials copied into evidence. It digests the user Codex configuration before and after the launch, refuses or reports on change, and records the digest among the receipt's protected surfaces. A test fails when a Codex exec argv is built outside the launcher. Removing existing stale entries stays a separate owner-authorized act.
affectedUsers: the operator (user-level Codex configuration and trust state for later sessions)
executors and verifiers running live Codex proofs or probes
suggestion.expectedValue: Live Codex proofs could satisfy an outside-portfolio clause by measurement instead of by waiver. D011's precondition would be enforced at the one place launches happen. With one argv instead of seven copies, later launch-policy changes land once.
suggestion.uncertainty: It is untested whether Codex authenticates, and keeps its trust writes confined, inside an isolated home without copying credentials; the diagnosis calls this a candidate to validate. Attribution of each historical entry to a specific launch is inference. Analogous user-level writes by the Claude or Copilot launches were not measured in this review.
risks: An isolated home may break authentication or drop user-level Codex settings the workers rely on
A refusing guard blocks live proofs until the launcher is validated
Consolidating seven launch sites touches probes that carry their own recorded qualification evidence
alternatives: A per-launch trust override for the scratch path, if Codex supports one, instead of an isolated home
Keep inheriting the home but add the before/after digest and report changes (detection without prevention)
Operator-authorized periodic cleanup of DotLn-family entries (treats the symptom; the diagnosis says it does not prevent recurrence)
